title: Specializing in the 1 HTML file game genre and Im loving it. Game is fully made with ascii characters.
author: OddSliceOfMarketing
selftext:
Every hill, river, roof and sheep in Land of ASCII \[0.6.5\] is drawn in letters, and so are the people of its three villages. It's a quiet game about exploring a small land, roughly 2 x 2 km, and the whole thing fits in one 1 MB HTML file. There are no images and no engine, and you play it in your browser.

There's a fort on a hill and a lake to walk to. The villagers go about their own days; say hello and some of them will ask you a small favour. Stop wherever the view is good and sketch it. Night falls, rain sets in and clears again, and the music and every sound are made in code as you walk.

Half an hour is enough to see the main sights. After that the land is still there whenever you want a calm walk, and each seed builds a different world.  
  


\- The whole game is one HTML file of about 1 MB (1,017 KB). No images, no engine, no downloads.

\- The world is 2 x 2 km. Walking straight across takes about 8 minutes.

\- Every frame is around 40,000 letters, drawn from 28 characters in 617 colours.

\- 32 kinds of sound and 3 music tracks, all made in code as you play. There isn't a single recording.

\- The default world has nearly 12,000 trees, 58 villagers, 255 animals and 59 buildings.

\- The villagers have 329 lines of dialogue between them.

\- 27,000 lines of code, with no libraries.

Anyone interested of trying it out? I can share the link if its okay.

comments.author: AnOnlineHandle
comments.body: The style looks nice. I'm curious, is it any faster to draw things this way than with meshes in WebGL? Or does it effectively require all the same calculations for lighting etc which have to be done in software?

replies.author: OddSliceOfMarketing
replies.body: Not faster, no. It's a CPU heightfield raycaster: one ray per screen column, lighting, shadows and water all in software across 8 workers, and WebGL only draws the finished character grid (about 0.1 ms). It works because the grid is 28–52k cells, not millions of pixels, so a frame is 5–9 ms and holds 60 fps. The text isn't a filter over a normal render; each cell picks its glyph from what the ray hit. A GPU mesh version would be faster, but this stays one HTML file with no libraries.

comments.author: BrianScottGregory
comments.body: I am more curious about the prompt and build setup, what did you use to create this?

replies.author: OddSliceOfMarketing
replies.body: Its quite elaborate, this is the 3rd attempt. I have a project that is fed lots of context engineering and is acting like a PM, that scopes the task. Then bite by bite I feed it to Claude Code, Opus 5.5 Extra. I constantly do back-and-forths, critial thinking and creativity is all mine. This is the work of a whole week - as well as "internal" beta testing from friends. This repo has 74 deployments.
